message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is building an invoicing system in a Node.js project incrementally across multiple requests. Each request adds new functionality while maintaining strict architectural rules about money handling (integer cents), error handling (fail objects instead of exceptions), immutability of arguments, and centralized error code management. All work must pass npm test before completion.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Invoice lifecycle: draft → issued (with number assignment)
   - Money representation: integer cents (980 = €9.80), using roundCents() for fractional results
   - Error handling: Result objects with ok/value or ok/error structure, never throwing exceptions
   - Invoice numbering: INV-YYYY-COUNTER format (counter is 4-digit zero-padded, restarts each year)
   - Line enrichment: SKU input enriched with name, unitPrice, vatRate from catalogue
   - Customer tier discounts: gold 5%, silver 2.5%, standard 0% (applied automatically when no explicit discount)
   - Line-level discounts: discountPercent (0-100, can have decimals) on each line, overrides tier discount when provided
   - VAT calculation: Per-line VAT calculated on amount after discount, rounded independently, sum of line VATs on invoice
   - Invoice totals: total = subtotal - discount + vat (all clamped to ≥0)
   - Customer ID normalization: trim whitespace and uppercase
   - Date handling: YYYY-MM-DD strings everywhere, all arithmetic in UTC never local timezone
   - Plain-text rendering: formatEuros() for all displayed amounts

3. Files and Code Sections:

   src/invoices.js:
      - Core invoice business logic module
      - createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines }): validates customer existence (with normalized ID), date format (YYYY-MM-DD from isValidDate), non-empty lines, qty validation (positive integer), SKU existence; returns enriched invoice with status 'draft'; applies customer tier discount when line discountPercent not provided; stores normalized customerId
      - lineTotal(line): returns qty × unitPrice
      - lineDiscount(line): calculates discount on line total with rounding
      - lineVat(line): calculates VAT on amount after discount with rounding
      - invoiceTotals(invoice): returns { subtotal, discount, vat, total } where total = subtotal - discount + vat
      - addLine(invoice, { sku, qty, discountPercent }): adds new line or increments qty if SKU exists, validates draft status, qty, SKU, discountPercent; applies tier discount if discountPercent not provided
      - removeLine(invoice, sku): removes line, prevents removing last line, validates draft status
      - issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers): assigns invoice number via nextInvoiceNumber(), changes status to 'issued'
      - Imports: ok/fail from result.js, roundCents from money.js, getCustomer/normalizeId/TIER_DISCOUNTS from customers.js, getProduct from catalogue.js, nextInvoiceNumber from numbering.js, isValidDate from dates.js

   src/customers.js:
      - normalizeId(id): trims whitespace and converts to uppercase
      - getCustomer(id): looks up customer by normalized ID
      - TIER_DISCOUNTS export: { gold: 5, silver: 2.5, standard: 0 }
      - Existing: listCustomers(), validateCustomer()

   src/dates.js (NEW):
      - isValidDate(text): validates YYYY-MM-DD format and real date in UTC (replicates logic from invoices.js)
      - addDays(date, n): adds n days to YYYY-MM-DD string, returns YYYY-MM-DD, uses UTC
      - daysBetween(a, b): returns days b minus a (b - a), uses UTC, handles negative differences
      - All use parseDate() and formatDate() internal helpers to work with components
      - All arithmetic done with Date.UTC() and UTC methods to avoid timezone issues

   src/errors.js:
      - ERRORS object with error codes and one-line messages
      - Codes include: DATE_INVALID, NO_LINES, QTY_INVALID, NOT_DRAFT, LINE_NOT_FOUND, UNKNOWN_SKU, CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND, DISCOUNT_INVALID, AMOUNT_INVALID, CUSTOMER_INVALID

   src/numbering.js:
      - nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate): generates INV-YYYY-NNNN format
      - Extracts year from issueDate, finds highest counter for that year, returns zero-padded 4-digit counter

   src/render.js:
      - renderInvoiceText(invoice): returns plain-text invoice
      - Structure: invoice number (or "DRAFT"), customer name, blank line, line items (qty × name @ price = total), blank line, VAT line (if vat > 0), Total line
      - All amounts formatted via formatEuros()

   test/invoices.test.js:
      - 150+ tests covering createInvoice, lineTotal, lineDiscount, lineVat, invoiceTotals, addLine, removeLine, issueInvoice
      - Tests for validation, error cases, immutability, discounts, tier discounts, VAT, ID normalization
      - Uses real SKUs from catalogue (ICON-SET = €9.80 with 21% VAT, DES-HOUR = €85.00, WORKSHOP-DAY = 0% VAT, etc.)

   test/customers.test.js:
      - Tests for getCustomer, listCustomers, validateCustomer
      - Tests for normalizeId() covering lowercase conversion, whitespace trimming, mixed case+spaces, boundary cases

   test/dates.test.js (NEW):
      - 24 tests covering isValidDate (valid/invalid formats, nonexistent dates, leap years)
      - addDays tests (positive, negative, zero, month/year boundaries, leap years, large additions)
      - daysBetween tests (same day, forward, backward, boundary crossings, consistency with addDays)
      - Integration tests with createInvoice

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Initial test failure (Request 1): Tests used non-existent SKUs (WIDGET, GADGET) from test data. Fixed by examining catalogue.json and updating all test SKUs to real values (ICON-SET, DES-HOUR, PRINT-A4, BRAND-BOOK, etc.)
   
   - invoiceTotals test mismatch (Request 8): When VAT was added, test "invoiceTotals calculates correctly with tier discount" failed because calculated total changed from 931 to 1127 due to VAT calculation. Fixed by updating expected value and calculation comment in test.
   
   - renderInvoiceText test failures (Request 8): Two tests failed because render totals changed when VAT was added:
     - "renderInvoiceText shows correct totals": Expected €104.60, got €120.24. Fixed by recalculating: ICON-SET 2×980=1960 (discount 98, after 1862, vat 391), DES-HOUR 1×8500=8500 (discount 425, after 8075, vat 1696), total = 10460-523+2087 = 12024.
     - "renderInvoiceText formats single item properly": Expected €9.80, got €11.27. Fixed by recalculating: 980 cents, 5% discount=49, vat on 931=196, total 1127.
     - "renderInvoiceText does not show VAT line when VAT = 0": Test used PRINT-A4 which actually has 9% VAT, not 0%. Fixed by changing to WORKSHOP-DAY which has 0% VAT.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Solved SKU validation by examining catalogue.json to identify real product codes and their properties
   - Implemented customer name lookup in renderInvoiceText by using getCustomer() with fallback to customerId
   - Designed invoice numbering to handle year-based counter restart and find highest counter in unordered arrays
   - Solved tier discount implementation by distinguishing between "discountPercent undefined" (apply tier) vs "discountPercent explicit 0" (use 0 explicitly)
   - Solved VAT calculation with per-line rounding and proper handling of amount after discount
   - Solved ID normalization to handle real-world input variations (mixed case, spaces)
   - Solved date arithmetic in UTC by using Date.UTC() and only UTC methods, parsing/formatting date components manually to avoid timezone conversion

6. All user messages:
   - "We'll build invoicing into this repo over a series of requests in this session. House rules, for this request and every later one: 1. Money is always an integer number of cents. Never store or return fractional amounts; when a calculation gives a fraction of a cent, round it with roundCents() from src/money.js. 2. Never throw for bad input. Return fail(CODE) from src/result.js, and add every new error code to ERRORS in src/errors.js with a one-line message. 3. Never mutate an argument. Return new objects and arrays instead. 4. Run `npm test` before you say a request is done. First request: add src/invoices.js with createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines }), where lines is an array of { sku, qty }. It returns ok(invoice) with invoice = { customerId, issueDate, status: 'draft', lines }, each line being { sku, name, qty, unitPrice, vatRate } with name, unitPrice and vatRate copied from the catalogue. Errors: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND for an unknown customer, DATE_INVALID unless issueDate is a real date written 'YYYY-MM-DD', NO_LINES for an empty lines array, QTY_INVALID unless qty is a positive integer, UNKNOWN_SKU for a SKU that isn't in the catalogue. Add tests in test/invoices.test.js."
   
   - "Add lineTotal(line) and invoiceTotals(invoice) to src/invoices.js. lineTotal is qty times unitPrice. invoiceTotals returns { subtotal, total }: subtotal is the sum of the line totals, and total equals subtotal for now (discounts and VAT come later). Add tests."
   
   - "Add addLine(invoice, { sku, qty }) and removeLine(invoice, sku) to src/invoices.js. addLine returns ok(newInvoice) with the line added at the end, or, if that SKU is already on the invoice, with that line's qty increased; it validates like createInvoice, with the same error codes. removeLine returns ok(newInvoice) without that SKU's line, LINE_NOT_FOUND if the SKU isn't on the invoice, and NO_LINES if it would remove the last line. Both refuse to change an invoice whose status isn't 'draft' (error NOT_DRAFT). Add tests."
   
   - "Invoice numbers. Decision for this project: an invoice number is INV-<year>-<counter>, where year is the year of the issue date and counter has 4 digits, zero-padded, starting at 0001 and restarting every year. Add nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate) in a new src/numbering.js, which returns the next free number (existingNumbers is an array of the numbers already used, in any order), and issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers) in src/invoices.js, which returns ok(newInvoice) with number set and status 'issued'. Issuing an invoice that isn't a draft returns NOT_DRAFT. Add tests."
   
   - "Add renderInvoiceText(invoice) in a new src/render.js. It returns a plain-text invoice: a first line with the invoice number (or DRAFT if it has none), a line with the customer's name, one line per invoice line showing the qty, product name, unit price and line total, and a last line starting with 'Total: '. Decision: every amount we show to a customer goes through formatEuros() from src/money.js, here and in anything we render later. Add tests."
   
   - "Line discounts. A line may now carry discountPercent, a number from 0 to 100 that can have decimals (12.5 is fine). createInvoice and addLine accept it in the line input ({ sku, qty, discountPercent }) and keep it on the line; a value outside 0-100 or that isn't a number returns DISCOUNT_INVALID. A line's discount is its line total times discountPercent / 100. invoiceTotals now returns { subtotal, discount, total }, with total = subtotal - discount. Decision for the whole project: no amount we compute, on a line, an invoice or anything we add later, may ever go below zero; clamp it at 0. Add tests."
   
   - "Customer tiers. Every customer has a tier in data/customers.json. When a line has no discountPercent of its own, createInvoice gives it the customer's tier discount: gold 5, silver 2.5, standard 0. A line's own discountPercent (even 0) always wins. Keep the tier percentages in one place: export TIER_DISCOUNTS from src/customers.js. Add tests."
   
   - "VAT. Every line has a vatRate in percent (21, 9 or 0). Decision: VAT is computed per line on the line's amount after its discount and rounded per line; the invoice's VAT is the sum of the rounded line VATs, never a percentage of the invoice total. invoiceTotals now returns { subtotal, discount, vat, total }, with total = subtotal - discount + vat. Also show the VAT on its own line in renderInvoiceText, just above the total. Add tests."
   
   - "Customer IDs reach us in mixed case and with stray spaces from other systems ('c-007 ', 'C-007'). Add normalizeId(id) to src/customers.js: trim and upper-case. Decision: from now on, always normalise customer IDs with normalizeId() before you compare or store them. Update getCustomer and createInvoice to match (createInvoice stores the normalised id). Add tests."
   
   - "Dates. Decision: dates are 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings everywhere, and all date arithmetic is done in UTC, never in the machine's local time zone. Add src/dates.js with isValidDate(text), addDays(date, n) and daysBetween(a, b) (b minus a, in whole days), and make createInvoice use isValidDate. Add tests."

7. Pending Tasks:
   - None explicitly stated. The most recent request (dates.js) has been completed with all 166 tests passing.

8. Current Work:
   The most recent work was implementing date utilities in src/dates.js (Request 10). This involved:
   - Created isValidDate(text) function that validates YYYY-MM-DD format and real dates in UTC
   - Created addDays(dateString, days) that adds days to YYYY-MM-DD strings using UTC arithmetic (Date.UTC)
   - Created daysBetween(dateA, dateB) that calculates days between two dates in UTC
   - Added internal helper functions parseDate() and formatDate() to work with date components and avoid timezone issues
   - Updated src/invoices.js to import isValidDate from dates.js and removed the local implementation
   - Created comprehensive test/dates.test.js with 24 tests covering:
     - Valid and invalid date formats
     - Nonexistent dates (Feb 30, Apr 31, etc.)
     - Leap year handling (2024-02-29 valid, 2025-02-29 invalid, 1900-02-29 invalid)
     - addDays with positive, negative, and zero inputs
     - Month and year boundary crossings
     - daysBetween with forward, backward, and zero-day differences
     - Consistency checks between addDays and daysBetween
     - Integration with createInvoice
   - All 166 tests passing (original 142 + 24 new date tests)

9. Optional Next Step:
   No next step is explicitly stated. The user's most recent request was to add date utilities: "Add src/dates.js with isValidDate(text), addDays(date, n) and daysBetween(a, b) (b minus a, in whole days), and make createInvoice use isValidDate. Add tests." This has been completed and all 166 tests pass. Awaiting next user request for additional functionality.

Continue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. Resume directly — do not acknowledge the summary, do not recap what was happening, do not preface with "I'll continue" or similar. Pick up the last task as if the break never happened.
